summary: PolarVista is evaluating Redwood for a media search and auto-captioning stack. Primary concerns: support for very long contexts (40k-150k tokens), multilingual fidelity (Spanish/Portuguese/Korean), deterministic outputs for editorial workflows, secure tool-calling to internal APIs, and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. Agreed next steps include a multi-model benchmark, security docs, and a Dedicated sizing proposal.
topics: Open model comparison (Llama 3 70B, Mistral 30B, MPT multilingual)
Context window strategies (single 64k/128k vs chunk+retrieval chaining)
Tool-calling patterns for caption-sync and metadata enrichment
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (latency, cost, residency, SLA)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-21 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20270521-polarvista-01
Attendees: Maya Santos (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Malik (Head of AI, PolarVista), Carlos Rivera (CTO), Nora Kim (ML Engineer)

[00:00] Maya Santos (Redwood AE): Thanks everyone for joining. Quick audio check?
[00:06] Aisha Malik (PolarVista): Yep can hear you.
[00:10] Carlos Rivera (CTO): Hello. Looking forward to this.
[00:15] Liam Chen (Redwood SE): I'll steer the tech bits after Maya does the intro.

[00:30] Aisha: Quick context: PolarVista indexes long-form audio, we surface time-coded captions, highlights, and auto-summaries. Users want instant preview for short clips but editorial workflows run nightly batch jobs. Editors need deterministic outputs — low hallucination, reproducible summaries.

[00:55] Nora Kim: We have Spanish/Portuguese heavy content and pockets of Korean/Japanese. A single asset can be 40k to 150k tokens when we include transcripts+metadata+prompt.

[01:18] Maya: When you say 150k, is that raw transcript tokens or combined prompt+instructions?

[01:24] Nora: Combined. We often attach a brief prompt and then the full transcript for QA or highlight extraction.

[01:40] Liam: Two axes: model context window and runtime ops (KV cache/prefix caching), and deployment mode. Hosted is fastest to start, Dedicated for predictable throughput and SLAs, Private for strict residency and on-prem needs.

[02:05] Carlos: Security is a must — no PII in logs, KMS integration, SSO, and audit logs for editorial changes.

[02:18] Maya: We'll share SOC2 and our VPC/KMS playbook; Private option details will be included.

[03:02] Aisha: On model choice: we prefer open models if they meet quality. Llama 3 70B looked good on few-shot summaries but cost/latency is a worry. Curious about Mistral 30Bis it editor-grade?

[03:25] Liam: Mistral 30B is strong for instruction following at lower cost. Llama 3 70B often gives better long-context behavior if tuned and run with the right kernels. MPT variants can help multilingual but Korean/Japanese are spotty.

[04:05] Nora: How do you handle very long context  do you stitch chunks or run a single large-window?

[04:12] Liam: Both. We can run single-window up to 128k on Dedicated with quantized weights and optimized KV. Hosted standard is 64k; larger windows are possible but usually need Dedicated/Private for throughput. Or use chunk+retrieval+chaining to reduce cost.

[04:40] Aisha: Retrieval+chaining might work for editorial where editors want full-context reasoning but not every token loaded at once.

[04:48] [transcription glitch, overlap]

[05:00] Carlos: On tool-calling: we have an internal caption-sync API and metadata enrichment service. Can Redwood call our services securely and enforce per-request RBAC?

[05:14] Liam: Yes. You can register tools, set signatures, and for Dedicated/Private we can operate in VPC with secure egress/mTLS. RBAC by route/service account is supported.

[05:40] Nora: Are tool outputs merged into the model output or kept as side-channel? Editors need to validate tool responses.

[05:52] Liam: Side-channel by default; logs and audit trails can capture inputs, tool call, and outputs. We can sign tool outputs for cryptographic proof if you want.

[06:10] Aisha: For multilingual, should we fine-tune or use adapters? We rotate models often.

[06:20] Liam: Recommend base multilingual model + small LoRA/PEFT adapters. Redwood supports loading adapters on Dedicated/Private so you can avoid full model retrain and keep rotation flexibility.

[07:00] Carlos: Latency targets: previews sub-500ms; batch jobs can be minutes. Can Redwood meet that split?

[07:12] Maya: Hosted handles low-latency short requests and streaming. Dedicated with reserved GPUs is the path for predictable sub-500ms at scale; we'll map QPS and tail SLOs in the POC.

[07:40] Nora: Cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated?

[07:48] Maya: Depends on utilization. Hosted cheaper for intermittent workloads; Dedicated with commits reduces per-token cost for steady throughput. We'll model your realtime vs batch mix.

[08:10] Aisha: Editors require determinism — same prompt+transcript => identical summary. Random sampling is a blocker.

[08:20] Liam: Deterministic decoding is available (greedy/fixed-seed). Some models/parallel kernels can complicate determinism; we'll validate during benchmark and provide output hashing/diffing to detect drift.

[09:20] Maya: Proposed POC: 1) small benchmark across 3 models (Llama 3 70B, Mistral 30B instruct, multilingual MPT) on Nora's samples; 2) tool-calling integration test with caption-sync; 3) week-long Dedicated trial for larger windows if needed.

[09:55] Carlos: What metrics will Redwood report?

[10:00] Liam: Token-level latency, per-route cost, ROUGE/BERTScore + editorial checklist, determinism metric (run-to-run divergence), traces for replay.

[10:30] Nora: Can Redwood cache recurring prefixes for repeated show intros?

[10:40] Liam: Yes — prefix/KV caching supported. Dedicated can pin cache persistence; Hosted uses TTLs.

[11:05] Aisha: EU data residency is required for some assets.

[11:12] Maya: We offer regional hosting and can run Private control planes in a customer VPC in eu-west-1; details in security pack.

[12:00] Carlos: For Private/on-prem, what's the minimal hardware for 64k vs 128k windows on Llama 3 70B?

[12:10] Liam: 128k typically needs multi-GPU nodes (NVLink) like 8xH100 with sharded KV; 64k can be 4xH100 depending on quantization. We'll include a sizing guide.

[12:40] Nora: Do you support 4-bit/8-bit quantized runtimes?

[12:46] Liam: Yes. Quantized paths supported, quality tradeoffs documented; we'll add a sensitivity report.

[13:10] Aisha: Integration detail: model calls caption-sync then writes result to S3 with metadata tags. Can Redwood sign those requests?

[13:20] Liam: Yes, mTLS and mutual auth, plus example connector you can deploy in your VPC.

[14:30] Maya: Posting POC checklist in chat: samples, acceptance criteria, QPS, prioritized languages, legal constraints.

[15:00] Nora: Priorities: Spanish and Portuguese first, then Korean. Acceptance: editorial pass >=90%, determinism with chosen config, caption sync success >99%.

[15:30] Carlos: Need contract language for data deletion and EU residency.

[15:36] Maya: We'll include standard DPA and deletion flow.

[16:30] Aisha: Previews must be read-only until an editor confirms. Can tool calls be read-only?

[16:40] Liam: Yes — preview vs write tools with separate service accounts, you control apply permissions.

[17:05] Nora: Pre-built CMS connectors?

[17:12] Liam: Templates and community connectors exist; custom adapters can be templated.

[18:20] Maya: Dedicated has SLA on committed capacity and latency tiers; Hosted is observability-first.

[19:00] Aisha: Target beta in Q3 if POC succeeds. Start POC in 2-3 weeks.

[19:12] Maya: We'll aim to start benchmarks within 48 hours of dataset receipt.

[34:00] Nora: For streaming tool-calls we need token-level alignment back to timestamps for captions.

[34:10] Liam: Streaming tokens can be aligned if you pass timing metadata; chunk boundaries need care.

[39:30] Aisha: Fallback policies: if Dedicated is overloaded can you downgrade to smaller model automatically?

[39:40] Liam: Yes, routing policies support fallback by latency/capacity with alerts so editors see degraded mode.

[45:00] Carlos: Will Redwood run blind editorial tests?

[45:08] Maya: Yes, part of the POC with a grading rubric.

[55:30] Maya: Recap: Redwood will run multi-model benchmark, share security/infra docs, provide Dedicated cost/size for 64k/128k, and schedule SE deep-dive on tool-calling.

[55:58] Aisha: We'll upload data tomorrow.

[61:38] (call ends)
